summary: Skeptical examination confirms the mathematical singleton-trace argument and the unrestricted-support two-star trace obstruction. The newly added singleton explanation needs a precise lift back to original four-set members: the residual triples are not themselves members of H. The frozen Lean theorem already makes the correct lift, so this is a minor prose repair, not a counterexample to the result.
required_revisions: In the Section 4 singleton-trace explanation, replace the claim that disjoint residues together with R give the forbidden sunflower by the precise statement that two disjoint residues make their original four-set members together with R a sunflower whose core is the common singleton.

findings.statement: The new sentence says disjoint residues together with R would form a sunflower. The residues are three-sets outside the original four-uniform family, so that sunflower alone is not forbidden by H being sunflower-free. The contradiction requires restoring the common singleton to both residues.
findings.disposition: Specify the original four-set members and their singleton core; Erdos20RankFour.singleton_trace_card_le_ten already proves the intended statement.

checks.scope: Adversarial check of the repaired singleton-trace dependency
checks.method: Reconstructed the trace argument for S intersect R = T intersect R = {a}, and inspected singleton_trace_card_le_ten plus MeetingDefect.lean.
checks.observation: Deletion of a is injective on the trace class and preserves sunflower-freeness. If the two residues are disjoint, then S intersect T = S intersect R = T intersect R = {a}; R is distinct from S and T because its intersection with either has size one rather than four. Hence the original members form the contradiction, and the residual family is intersecting. The source carries this argument correctly; the new prose omits the restoration step and should be repaired as requested.

checks.scope: Hidden support and center assumptions in the two-star trace lemma
checks.method: Adversarially followed Section 3.1 with a residual row having exactly two points outside U and with no ambient support bound, tracking both centers and the disjoint union cardinality.
checks.observation: Non-cooccurrence ensures every y-star member avoids x and ensures y is outside U. Since a residual row avoids y, disjointness from a y-star member would put at least its two outside-U points plus y into an eight-point union that must have at least six points in U, a contradiction. This works even with arbitrary additional ambient points. Both centers are excluded from U and V before the noncenter degree cap is used; no hidden support bound or extra high-point hypothesis is required.
